module Types
  class BaseObject < GraphQL::Schema::Object
    def self.field(*args, **kwargs, &)
      super

      # The old api contained non-camelized fields
      # We want to support these for now, but throw a deprecation warning
      #
      # Example:
      # proposal_notifications => Deprecation warning (Old api)
      # proposalNotifications => No deprecation warning (New api)
      field_name = args[0]

      if field_name.to_s.include?("_")
        reason = "Snake case fields are deprecated. Please use #{field_name.to_s.camelize(:lower)}."
        super(*args, **kwargs.merge({ camelize: false, deprecation_reason: reason }), &)
      end

      # Make sure associations only return public records
      # by automatically calling 'public_for_api'
      type_class = args[1]

      if type_class.is_a?(Class) && type_class.ancestors.include?(GraphQL::Types::Relay::BaseConnection)
        define_method(field_name) { object.send(field_name).public_for_api }
      end
    end

    def self.object_by_id_field(field_name, type, description, null:)
      field field_name, type, description, null: null do
        argument :id, ID, required: true, default_value: false
      end
    end

    def self.collection_field(field_name, type, ...)
      field(field_name, type.connection_type, ...)
    end
  end
end

module Types
  class BaseObject < GraphQL::Schema::Object
    def self.field(*args, **kwargs, &)
      super

      # The old api contained non-camelized fields
      # We want to support these for now, but throw a deprecation warning
      #
      # Example:
      # proposal_notifications => Deprecation warning (Old api)
      # proposalNotifications => No deprecation warning (New api)
      field_name = args[0]

      if field_name.to_s.include?("_")
        reason = "Snake case fields are deprecated. Please use #{field_name.to_s.camelize(:lower)}."
        super(*args, **kwargs.merge({ camelize: false, deprecation_reason: reason }), &)
      end

      # Make sure associations only return public records
      # by automatically calling 'public_for_api'
      type_class = args[1]

      if type_class.is_a?(Class) && type_class.ancestors.include?(GraphQL::Types::Relay::BaseConnection)
        define_method(field_name) { object.send(field_name).public_for_api }
      end
    end

    def self.object_by_id_field(field_name, type, description, null:)
      field field_name, type, description, null: null do
        argument :id, ID, required: true, default_value: false
      end
    end

    def self.collection_field(field_name, type, ...)
      field(field_name, type.connection_type, ...)
    end
  end
end

When websites are designed with accessibility in mind, all users can access content in equal conditions, for example:

  • Providing alternative text to the images, blind or visually impaired users can use special readers to access the information.
  • When videos have subtitles, users with hearing difficulties can fully understand them.
  • If the contents are written in a simple and illustrated language, users with learning problems are better able to understand them.
  • If the user has mobility problems and it is difficult to use the mouse, the alternatives with the keyboard help in navigation.

Keyboard shortcuts

To be able to navigate through this website in an accessible way, a group of quick access keys has been programmed that gather the main sections of general interest in which the site is organized.

Keyboard shortcuts for the navigation menu

Browser Key combination

Firefox ALT + CAPS + shortcut

Safari ALT + shortcut (CMD + shortcut for MAC)

Text size

The accessible design of this website allows the user to choose the size of the text that suits him. This action can be carried out in different ways depending on the browser used.

Browser Action to be taken
Explorer View > Text size
Firefox View > Size
Chrome Settings (icon) > Options > Advanced > Web Content > Text size
Safari View > Zoom In/Zoom out
Opera View > scale

Another way to modify the text size is to use the keyboard shortcuts defined in browsers, in particular the key combination:

  • CTRL and + (CMD and + on MAC) Increases text size
  • CTRL and - (CMD and - on MAC) Decreases text size

module Ahoy
  class DataSource
    def self.build(&block)
      new.tap { |data_source| block.call(data_source) }.build
    end

    # Adds a collection with the datasource
    # Name is the name of the collection and will be showed in the
    # chart
    def add(name, collection)
      collections.push data: collection, name: name
      dates.merge(collection.keys)
    end

    def build
      data = { x: [] }
      dates.sort.each do |date|
        # Add the key with a valid date format
        data[:x].push date.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")

        # Add the value for each column, or 0 if not present
        collections.each do |col|
          data[col[:name]] ||= []
          count = col[:data][date] || 0
          data[col[:name]].push count
        end
      end

      data
    end

    private

      def collections
        @collections ||= []
      end

      def dates
        @dates ||= Set.new
      end
  end
end

      format.any { render json: consul_installation_details.to_json, content_type: "application/json" }
    end
  end

  private

    def consul_installation_details
      { release: "2.6.0" }.merge(features: settings_feature_flags)
    end

    def settings_feature_flags
      Setting.where("key LIKE 'process.%'")
             .pluck(:key, :value)
             .to_h
             .transform_keys { |key| key.remove("process.") }
    end
end

messages.thinking:
**Analyzing Potential Impacts of Retired Citizen Proposal Settings**

Okay, here's what's running through my mind. I've spotted three critical areas affected by the deprecation of citizen proposals. First, the `Ahoy::Chart.event_names_with_collections` method, which is used in `/admin/stats`, could crash if it still included references to `Proposal.with_hidden`. Good thing that's been addressed, but it highlights the need to be thorough.

Secondly, I see an issue with `Milestone.public_for_api`, which uses `Proposal.public_for_api`. I'll want to investigate how it interacts with the retired proposal data and ensure there are no inconsistencies there.

The third, and most pressing, concern revolves around `InstallationController#settings_feature_flags` and the `Setting` model. I'm focusing on the `process.proposals` setting and how its removal in Deploy 2 affects Deploy 1 (which will be live concurrently). I need to ensure that the `/consul.json` endpoint doesn't incorrectly report `process.proposals` as active in Deploy 1, even though it's been deprecated.

Initially, I considered a transitional `default_scope` on the `Setting` model in Deploy 1-2 to exclude the retired keys. This seemed like a good solution on the surface, but I need to think this through. Specifically, I need to make sure I don't introduce any conflicts with the `uniqueness: true` validation on the `Setting` key. I'll make a list of *every* retired citizen-proposal setting key to make sure I've got everything:

*   `feature.featured_proposals`
*   `feature.user.recommendations_on_proposals`
*   `feature.dashboard.notification_emails`
*   `homepage.widgets.feeds.proposals`
*   `process.proposals`
*   `proposals.successful_proposal_id`
*   `proposals.poll_short_title`
*   `proposals.poll_description`
*   `proposals.poll_link`
*   `proposals.email_short_title`
*   `proposals.email_description`
*   `proposals.poster_short_title`
*   `proposals.poster_description`
*   `months_to_archive_proposals`
*   `proposal_notification_minimum_interval_in_days`
*   `featured_proposals_number`
*   `sdg.process.proposals`

(Note: `proposal_code_prefix`, `max_votes_for_proposal_edit`, and `votes_for_proposal_success` are *staying* because `Legislation::Proposal` still uses them).

I've determined that in Deploy 1, those 17 rows will still exist in the database, so Deploy 0 servers will continue to function. But on Deploy 1 servers, `Setting["process.proposals"]` should return `nil`. Now, what if a test calls `Setting.reset_defaults`, which will no longer include the removed keys? Or, what if someone manually tries to set `Setting["process.proposals"] = true`?

Using a `default_scope` would cause problems if it tried to write a key that's already in the database and filtered out by that scope.

Instead of `default_scope`, I'm going to modify `InstallationController#settings_feature_flags`. I'll filter `.where.not(key: "process.proposals")` (or `Setting.defaults.keys.grep(/\Aprocess\./)`) instead, and *remove* all callers of `feature?(:proposals)` and the like from the code in Deploy 1. This would be a safer way to prevent conflicts while ensuring that `/consul.json` immediately omits `"proposals"` in Deploy 1 while maintaining compatibility with Deploy 0.

So in `InstallationController#settings_feature_flags`, I'll filter by `.where(key: %w[process.debates process.polls process.budgets process.legislation])` or `.where.not(key: "process.proposals")`. This way, there's *zero* risk of uniqueness collision, and `/consul.json` in Deploy 1 will immediately omit `"proposals"` while Deploy 0 still sees `process.proposals = "t"`. The `.where.not` filter will be removed in Deploy 3, after Deploy 2 deletes the settings in the DB.

Okay, now let me check `app/views/robots/index.text.erb` and then check the output of a `grep`

class Geozone < ApplicationRecord
  include Graphqlable

  attribute :color, default: "#0000ff"

  has_many :proposals
  has_many :debates
  has_many :users
  has_many :headings, class_name: "Budget::Heading", dependent: :nullify
  validates :name, presence: true
  validates :geojson, geojson_format: true

  scope :public_for_api, -> { all }

  def self.names
    Geozone.pluck(:name)
  end

  def safe_to_destroy?
    Geozone.reflect_on_all_associations(:has_many).all? do |association|
      association.klass.where(geozone: self).empty?
    end
  end

  def outline_points
    normalized_geojson&.to_json
  end

  private

    def normalized_geojson
      if geojson.present?
        parsed_geojson = JSON.parse(geojson)

        if parsed_geojson["type"] == "FeatureCollection"
          parsed_geojson["features"].each do |feature|
            feature["properties"] ||= {}
          end

          parsed_geojson
        elsif parsed_geojson["type"] == "Feature"
          parsed_geojson["properties"] ||= {}

          wrap_in_feature_collection(parsed_geojson)
        elsif parsed_geojson["geometry"]
          parsed_geojson["properties"] ||= {}

          wrap_in_feature_collection(wrap_in_feature(parsed_geojson["geometry"]))
        elsif parsed_geojson["type"] && parsed_geojson["coordinates"]
          wrap_in_feature_collection(wrap_in_feature(parsed_geojson))
        else
          raise ArgumentError, "Invalid GeoJSON fragment"
        end
      end
    end

    def wrap_in_feature(geometry)
      {
        type: "Feature",
        geometry: geometry,
        properties: {}
      }
    end

    def wrap_in_feature_collection(feature)
      {
        type: "FeatureCollection",
        features: [feature]
      }
    end
end

class I18nContent < ApplicationRecord
  validates :key, uniqueness: true

  translates :value, touch: true
  globalize_accessors

  # flat_hash returns a flattened hash, a hash with a single level of
  # depth in which each key is composed from the keys of the original
  # hash (whose value is not a hash) by typing in the key of the route
  # from the first level of the original hash
  #
  # Examples:
  #
  # hash = {
  #   'key1' => 'value1',
  #   'key2' => { 'key3' => 'value2',
  #               'key4' => { 'key5' => 'value3' } }
  # }
  #
  # I18nContent.flat_hash(hash) = {
  #   'key1' => 'value1',
  #   'key2.key3' => 'value2',
  #   'key2.key4.key5' => 'value3'
  # }
  #
  # I18nContent.flat_hash(hash, 'string') = {
  #   'string.key1' => 'value1',
  #   'string.key2.key3' => 'value2',
  #   'string.key2.key4.key5' => 'value3'
  # }
  #
  # I18nContent.flat_hash(hash, 'string', { 'key6' => 'value4' }) = {
  #   'key6' => 'value4',
  #   'string.key1' => 'value1',
  #   'string.key2.key3' => 'value2',
  #   'string.key2.key4.key5' => 'value3'
  # }

  def self.flat_hash(input, path = nil, output = {})
    return output.update({ path => input }) unless input.is_a? Hash

    input.map { |key, value| flat_hash(value, [path, key].compact.join("."), output) }
    output
  end

  def self.content_for(tab)
    translations_for(tab).map do |string|
      I18nContent.find_or_initialize_by(key: string)
    end
  end

  def self.translations_for(tab)
    if tab.to_s == "basic"
      basic_translations
    elsif tab.to_s == "machine_learning"
      machine_learning_translations
    else
      flat_hash(translations_hash_for(tab)).keys
    end
  end

  def self.translations_hash_for(tab)
    I18n.backend.send(:init_translations) unless I18n.backend.initialized?

    I18n.backend.send(:translations)[I18n.locale].select do |key, _translations|
      key.to_s == tab.to_s
    end
  end

  def self.basic_translations
    %w[
      debates.index.section_footer.title
      debates.index.section_footer.description
      debates.index.section_footer.help_text_1
      debates.index.section_footer.help_text_2
      debates.new.info
      debates.new.info_link
      debates.new.more_info
      debates.new.recommendation_one
      debates.new.recommendation_two
      debates.new.recommendation_three
      debates.new.recommendation_four
      debates.new.recommendations_title
      proposals.index.section_footer.title
      proposals.index.section_footer.description
      proposals.new.more_info
      proposals.new.recommendation_one
      proposals.new.recommendation_two
      proposals.new.recommendation_three
      proposals.new.recommendations_title
      polls.index.section_footer.title
      polls.index.section_footer.description
      legislation.processes.index.section_footer.title
      legislation.processes.index.section_footer.description
      budgets.index.section_footer.title
      budgets.index.section_footer.description
    ]
  end

  def self.machine_learning_translations
    %w[
      admin.machine_learning.title
      machine_learning.comments_summary
      machine_learning.info_text
      admin.machine_learning.comments_summary
      admin.machine_learning.comments_summary_description
      admin.machine_learning.related_content
      admin.machine_learning.related_content_description
      admin.machine_learning.tags
      admin.machine_learning.tags_description
    ]
  end

  def self.translations_hash(locale)
    Rails.cache.fetch(translation_class.where(locale: locale)) do
      all.to_h do |content|
        [content.key, translation_class.find_by(i18n_content_id: content, locale: locale)&.value]
      end
    end
  end

  def self.update(contents, enabled_translations = Setting.enabled_locales)
    contents.each do |content|
      values = content[:values].slice(*translation_params(enabled_translations))

      unless values.empty?
        values.each do |key, value|
          locale = key.split("_").last

          if value.match(/translation missing/)
            next
          elsif value == I18n.t(content[:id], locale: locale)
            Globalize.with_locale(locale) do
              I18nContent.find_by(key: content[:id])&.update!(value: value)
            end
          else
            text = I18nContent.find_or_create_by!(key: content[:id])
            Globalize.with_locale(locale) do
              text.update!(value: value)
            end
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end

  def self.translation_params(enabled_translations)
    translated_attribute_names.product(enabled_translations).map do |attr_name, loc|
      localized_attr_name_for(attr_name, loc)
    end
  end
end

  def self.update(contents, enabled_translations = Setting.enabled_locales)
    contents.each do |content|
      values = content[:values].slice(*translation_params(enabled_translations))

      unless values.empty?
        values.each do |key, value|
          locale = key.split("_").last

          if value.match(/translation missing/)
            next
          elsif value == I18n.t(content[:id], locale: locale)
            Globalize.with_locale(locale) do
              I18nContent.find_by(key: content[:id])&.update!(value: value)
            end
          else
            text = I18nContent.find_or_create_by!(key: content[:id])
            Globalize.with_locale(locale) do
              text.update!(value: value)
            end
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end

  def self.translation_params(enabled_translations)
    translated_attribute_names.product(enabled_translations).map do |attr_name, loc|
      localized_attr_name_for(attr_name, loc)
    end

messages.thinking:
**My Plan for a Clean and Methodical File Edit**

Okay, time to get to work. I need to make these edits to the codebase, and I'm going to do it cleanly and methodically, group by group. Let's start with **Group A**: Routes, Initializers, Sitemap, Rake Tasks, and Assets.

First, I'll go through each file in Group A and address the specific changes. For `config/routes.rb`, I'll remove the `draw :proposal` line. Then, I'll move to `config/routes/admin.rb` and clean it up. I need to remove several resource definitions for "proposals" and related notifications, which will be the primary focus of my work here. Under `resources :system_emails`, I'll keep only the `get :view` action and remove the others. I'll remove `get :proposal_notifications` and the `namespace :dashboard`. Next, `config/routes/moderation.rb` needs the proposal-related resources removed. The same goes for `config/routes/management.rb` and `config/routes/notification.rb`, which are also going to have some proposal related resources removed.

Moving on to `config/initializers`, I'll make some specific tweaks. In `acts_as_taggable_on.rb`, I need to add a transitional `default_scope` to exclude "Proposal" and update scopes, but I'll need to remember to remove those in Deploy 3. I'll also add `ignored_columns` for `proposals_count` in `Tag.class_eval`, which I'll also have to remove later. Similarly, in `vote_extensions.rb`, I'll add a transitional `default_scope` to exclude proposals, with a removal flag in Deploy 3, and adjust the public scope to include the appropriate objects.

I'll then remove the `if Setting["process.proposals"] ... end` block from `config/sitemap.rb`. In `lib/tasks/votes.rake`, I need to update the models used in `reset_hot_score`. Now, for the asset files: `app/assets/config/manifest.js` will need to have some references removed. In `app/assets/javascripts/application.js`, I'll remove an initialization call. And finally, I need to remove certain imports from `app/assets/stylesheets/application.scss` and CSS rules in `app/assets/stylesheets/widgets/feeds/participation.scss`.

Once I've made these edits, I'll use Ruby scripts to apply these changes. It's cleaner and less prone to errors than complex `sed` commands, so I'll be able to work quickly here. And of course, I'll verify everything with a `git diff` on Group A to ensure I haven't made any mistakes.

arguments.command:
cd /app && ruby -e '
# 1. config/routes.rb
File.write("config/routes.rb", File.read("config/routes.rb").sub("    draw :proposal\n", ""))

# 2. config/routes/admin.rb
admin_routes = File.read("config/routes/admin.rb")
admin_routes.sub!(/\n    resources :proposals, only: \[:index, :show, :update\] do.*?\n    end\n/m, "\n")
admin_routes.sub!(/\n    resources :hidden_proposals, only: :index do.*?\n    end\n/m, "\n")
admin_routes.sub!(/\n    resources :hidden_proposal_notifications, only: :index do.*?\n    end\n/m, "\n")

class RemoteTranslation < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :remote_translatable, polymorphic: true

  validates :remote_translatable_id, presence: true
  validates :remote_translatable_type, presence: true
  validates :locale, presence: true
  validates :locale, inclusion: { in: ->(_) { RemoteTranslations::Caller.available_locales }}
  validate :already_translated_resource
  after_commit :enqueue_remote_translation, on: :create

  def enqueue_remote_translation
    remote_caller.delay.call
  end

  def self.for(*)
    resources_groups(*).flatten.select { |resource| translation_empty?(resource) }.map do |resource|
      new(remote_translatable: resource, locale: I18n.locale)
    end
  end

  def self.resources_groups(*args)
    feeds = args.find { |arg| arg&.first.class == Widget::Feed } || []

    args.compact - [feeds] + feeds.map(&:items)
  end

  def self.translation_empty?(resource)
    resource.class.translates? && resource.translations.where(locale: I18n.locale).empty?
  end

  def self.create_all(remote_translations_params)
    remote_translations_params.map do |remote_translation_params|
      new(remote_translation_params)
    end.reject(&:already_translated?).reject(&:enqueued?).each(&:save!)
  end

  def already_translated_resource
    if already_translated?
      errors.add(:locale, :already_translated)
    end
  end

  def enqueued?
    self.class.where(remote_translatable: remote_translatable,
                     locale: locale,
                     error_message: nil).any?
  end

  def already_translated?
    remote_translatable&.translations&.where(locale: locale).present?
  end

  def remote_caller
    @remote_caller ||= RemoteTranslations::Caller.new(self)
  end
end

class RemoteTranslation < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :remote_translatable, polymorphic: true

  validates :remote_translatable_id, presence: true
  validates :remote_translatable_type, presence: true
  validates :locale, presence: true
  validates :locale, inclusion: { in: ->(_) { RemoteTranslations::Caller.available_locales }}
  validate :already_translated_resource
  after_commit :enqueue_remote_translation, on: :create

  def enqueue_remote_translation
    remote_caller.delay.call
  end

  def self.for(*)
    resources_groups(*).flatten.select { |resource| translation_empty?(resource) }.map do |resource|
      new(remote_translatable: resource, locale: I18n.locale)
    end
  end

  def self.resources_groups(*args)
    feeds = args.find { |arg| arg&.first.class == Widget::Feed } || []

    args.compact - [feeds] + feeds.map(&:items)
  end

  def self.translation_empty?(resource)
    resource.class.translates? && resource.translations.where(locale: I18n.locale).empty?
  end

  def self.create_all(remote_translations_params)
    remote_translations_params.map do |remote_translation_params|
      new(remote_translation_params)
    end.reject(&:already_translated?).reject(&:enqueued?).each(&:save!)
  end

  def already_translated_resource
    if already_translated?
      errors.add(:locale, :already_translated)
    end
  end

  def enqueued?
    self.class.where(remote_translatable: remote_translatable,
                     locale: locale,
                     error_message: nil).any?
  end

  def already_translated?
    remote_translatable&.translations&.where(locale: locale).present?
  end

  def remote_caller
    @remote_caller ||= RemoteTranslations::Caller.new(self)
  end
end

class Admin::SystemEmailsController < Admin::BaseController
  before_action :load_system_email, only: [:view]

  def index
    @system_emails = {
      budget_investment_created: %w[view edit_info],
      budget_investment_selected: %w[view edit_info],
      budget_investment_unfeasible: %w[view edit_info],
      budget_investment_unselected: %w[view edit_info],
      comment: %w[view edit_info],
      reply: %w[view edit_info],
      direct_message_for_receiver: %w[view edit_info],
      direct_message_for_sender: %w[view edit_info],
      email_verification: %w[view edit_info],
      user_invite: %w[view edit_info],
      evaluation_comment: %w[view edit_info]
    }
  end

  def view
    case @system_email
    when /\Abudget_investment/
      load_sample_investment
    when /\Adirect_message/
      load_sample_direct_message
    when "comment"
      load_sample_comment
    when "reply"
      load_sample_reply
    when "email_verification"
      load_sample_user
    when "user_invite"
      @subject = t("mailers.user_invite.subject", org_name: Setting["org_name"])
    when "evaluation_comment"
      load_sample_valuation_comment
    end
  end

  private

    def load_system_email
      @system_email = params[:system_email_id]
    end

    def load_sample_investment
      if Budget::Investment.any?
        @investment = Budget::Investment.last
        @subject = t("mailers.#{@system_email}.subject", code: @investment.code)
      else
        redirect_to admin_system_emails_path, alert: t("admin.system_emails.alert.no_investments")
      end
    end

    def load_sample_comment
      @comment = Comment.where(commentable_type: %w[Debate Budget::Investment]).last
      if @comment
        @commentable = @comment.commentable
        @subject = t("mailers.comment.subject", commentable: commentable_name)
      else
        redirect_to admin_system_emails_path, alert: t("admin.system_emails.alert.no_comments")
      end
    end

    def load_sample_reply
      reply = Comment.select(&:reply?).last
      if reply
        @email = ReplyEmail.new(reply)
      else
        redirect_to admin_system_emails_path, alert: t("admin.system_emails.alert.no_replies")
      end
    end

    def load_sample_valuation_comment
      comment = Comment.where(commentable_type: "Budget::Investment").last
      if comment
        @email = EvaluationCommentEmail.new(comment)
        @email_to = @email.to.first || current_user
      else
        redirect_to admin_system_emails_path,
                    alert: t("admin.system_emails.alert.no_evaluation_comments")
      end
    end

    def load_sample_user
      @user = User.last
      @token = @user.email_verification_token || SecureRandom.hex
      @subject = t("mailers.email_verification.subject")
    end

    def load_sample_direct_message
      @direct_message = DirectMessage.new(sender: current_user, receiver: current_user,
                                          title: t("admin.system_emails.message_title"),
                                          body: t("admin.system_emails.message_body"))
      @subject = t("mailers.#{@system_email}.subject")
    end

    def commentable_name
      t("activerecord.models.#{@commentable.class.name.underscore}", count: 1)
    end
end
EOF

messages.thinking:
**My I18n Task List**

Okay, time to tackle this i18n cleanup. First things first: I need to open `config/i18n-tasks.yml`. Right, I see the `ignore_missing` and `ignore_unused` sections. Let's start with `ignore_missing`. I'm going to remove `"activerecord.models.proposal"` and `"activerecord.errors.models.proposal_notification.*"` from that list. They are no longer needed.

Now for the `ignore_unused` section. I need to get rid of a few things here as well. I'll remove: `"admin.hidden_proposals.index.filter*"` ,`"admin.hidden_proposal_notifications.index.filter*"` ,`"admin.dashboard.administrator_tasks.index.filter*"` and `"admin.dashboard.actions.index.default*"`. Wait, hang on... I need to *keep* `"moderation.proposals.index.filter*"` and `"moderation.proposals.index.orders.*"` because `Moderation::Shared::IndexComponent` relies on `"moderation.proposals.index.*"` for `Legislation::Proposal` moderation. Okay, got it.

Moving on, I will remove these as well: `"moderation.proposal_notifications.index.filter*"` , `"moderation.proposal_notifications.index.orders.*"`, `"dashboard.recommended_actions.*"`, `"proposals.index.orders.*"`, `"proposals.index.section_header.*"`, and `"dashboard.polls.*.submit"`.

And there's something else I need to keep in mind: the wildcard entries! I see lines 139, 158, 164, 168, 186, 196, 202, 222, 225 have `"activerecord.*"`, `"admin.activity.show.filter*"`, `"admin.hidden_comments.index.hidden_*"`, `"admin.homepage.*"`, `"users.show.filters.*"`, `"notifications.notification.action.*"`, `"shared.suggest.*"`, `"related_content.content_title.*"`, and `"sdg_management.relations.index.filter*"` - which means I need to manually check the `config/locales/en/*.yml` files for any citizen-proposal-specific keys under those namespaces and clean them up too!

So, to summarize, I'll update `config/i18n-tasks.yml`, then run `bundle exec i18n-tasks missing` and `bundle exec i18n-tasks unused` to confirm the changes and get the full list of remaining items. That should give me a nice, clean list to work from.

cd /app && ruby -e '
c = File.read("config/i18n-tasks.yml")
[
  "  - \"activerecord.models.proposal\"\n",
  "  - \"activerecord.errors.models.proposal_notification.*\"\n",
  "  - \"admin.hidden_proposals.index.filter*\"\n",
  "  - \"admin.hidden_proposal_notifications.index.filter*\"\n",
  "  - \"admin.dashboard.administrator_tasks.index.filter*\"\n",
  "  - \"admin.dashboard.actions.index.default.*\"\n",
  "  - \"moderation.proposal_notifications.index.filter*\"\n",
  "  - \"moderation.proposal_notifications.index.orders.*\"\n",
  "  - \"dashboard.recommended_actions.*\"\n",
  "  - \"proposals.index.orders.*\"\n",
  "  - \"proposals.index.section_header.*\"\n",
  "  - \"dashboard.polls.*.submit\"\n"
].each { |l| raise "Missing #{l}" unless c.sub!(l, "") }
File.write("config/i18n-tasks.yml", c)
' && bundle exec i18n-tasks missing && (bundle exec i18n-tasks unused | head -n 60; true)

**Cleaning Up Redundant Translations**

Okay, so I've just realized something pretty clever. It looks like the `SDGManagement::MenuComponent` relies on dynamically generated I18n keys using `t("sdg_management.menu.#{relatable}")`, and the `i18n-tasks` gem, bless its heart, interprets that wildcard perfectly, as long as it's included as part of the related `sdg_management.menu.*` keys! Now that `"Proposal"` has been nixed from `SDG::Related::RELATABLE_TYPES`, that means we can safely remove the corresponding translation keys, specifically `sdg_management.menu.proposals`, without breaking anything.

Right, time to get rid of those stale keys in `config/locales/en/*.yml`. I'm thinking YAML-safe Ruby is the way to go to automate this cleanup across the board. That should handle all the files.

Hold on, before I get too trigger-happy, let's take a closer look at `config/locales/en/activerecord.yml` and `config/locales/en/settings.yml` first. Need to make absolutely sure we're not accidentally deleting something that's still relevant, like translations for `legislation/proposal` or any shared setting keys. Better safe than sorry.

cd /app && ruby -e '
require "yaml"

def delete_path(hash, *keys)
  last = keys.pop
  target = keys.reduce(hash) { |h, k| h.is_a?(Hash) ? h[k] : nil }
  target.delete(last) if target.is_a?(Hash)
end

# Using i18n-tasks data API keeps exact formatting matching i18n-tasks normalize!
' && bundle exec ruby -e '
require "i18n/tasks"
task = I18n::Tasks::BaseTask.new
keys_to_remove = %w[
  en.activerecord.attributes.dashboard/action
  en.activerecord.attributes.dashboard/administrator_task
  en.activerecord.attributes.link
  en.activerecord.attributes.proposal
  en.activerecord.attributes.proposal/translation
  en.activerecord.attributes.proposal_notification
  en.activerecord.attributes.user.email_digest

  en.activerecord.models.link
  en.activerecord.models.proposal
  en.activerecord.models.proposal_notification
  en.moderation.proposal_notifications
  en.admin.activity.show.filters.on_proposals
  en.admin.activity.show.filters.on_system_emails
  en.admin.banners.index.filters.proposals
  en.admin.hidden_comments.index.hidden_proposal
  en.admin.homepage.feeds.proposals

  en.admin.segment_recipient.all_proposal_authors

  en.notifications.notification.action.proposal_notification
  en.related_content.content_title.proposal
  en.users.show.filters.proposals
  en.welcome.feed.most_active.proposals
  en.welcome.feed.no_items.proposals

  en.welcome.recommended.proposals
  en.sdg_management.menu.proposals
  en.mailers.new_actions_notification_on_create
  en.mailers.new_actions_notification_on_published
  en.mailers.proposal_notification_digest
]
# Expand subtree keys so remove_by_key removes whole branches cleanly
all_leaves = []
task.data["en"].leaves do |node|
  full = node.full_key
  if keys_to_remove.any? { |prefix| full == prefix || full.start_with?("#{prefix}.") }
    all_leaves << full
  end
end
puts "Removing #{all_leaves.size} wildcard-hidden keys"
task.data.remove_by_key!(all_leaves)

  end

    fill_in "Text", with: options[:body] || "This is the notification body"
    fill_in :admin_notification_link, with: options[:link] || "https://www.decide.madrid.es/vota"
  end
end

require "rails_helper"

describe Shared::MapLocationComponent do
  describe "remove marker button" do
    it "is not rendered when there's no form" do
      map_location = build(:map_location, proposal: Proposal.new)

      render_inline Shared::MapLocationComponent.new(map_location)

      expect(page).not_to have_button "Remove map marker"
    end

    it "is not rendered when there's no mappable" do
      map_location = build(:map_location)
      form = ConsulFormBuilder.new(:map_location, map_location, ApplicationController.new.view_context, {})

      render_inline Shared::MapLocationComponent.new(map_location, form: form)

      expect(page).not_to have_button "Remove map marker"
    end

    it "is rendered when there's a form and a mappable" do
      map_location = build(:map_location, proposal: Proposal.new)
      form = ConsulFormBuilder.new(:map_location, map_location, ApplicationController.new.view_context, {})

      render_inline Shared::MapLocationComponent.new(map_location, form: form)

      expect(page).to have_button "Remove map marker"
    end
  end

  describe "marker title" do
    it "uses the coordinates when there's a mappable" do
      map_location = build(
        :map_location,
        proposal: Proposal.new(title: "Meet me here"),
        latitude: "25.25",
        longitude: "13.14"
      )

      render_inline Shared::MapLocationComponent.new(map_location)

      expect(page).to have_css "[data-marker-title='Latitude: 25.25. Longitude: 13.14']"
    end

    it "uses the coordinates when there's no mappable" do
      map_location = build(:map_location, latitude: "25.25", longitude: "13.14")

      render_inline Shared::MapLocationComponent.new(map_location)

      expect(page).to have_css "[data-marker-title='Latitude: 25.25. Longitude: 13.14']"
    end

    it "is not present when the map location isn't available" do
      map_location = build(:map_location, latitude: "25.25", longitude: nil)

      render_inline Shared::MapLocationComponent.new(map_location)

      expect(page).not_to have_css "[data-marker-title]"
    end
  end
end

describe SDGManagement::MenuComponent do
  let(:component) { SDGManagement::MenuComponent.new }

  before do
    Setting["feature.sdg"] = true
    Setting["sdg.process.budgets"] = true
    Setting["sdg.process.debates"] = true
    Setting["sdg.process.legislation"] = true
    Setting["sdg.process.polls"] = true
    Setting["sdg.process.proposals"] = true
  end

      expect(page).to have_link "Participatory budgets"
      expect(page).to have_link "Debates"
      expect(page).to have_link "Legislation processes"
      expect(page).to have_link "Legislation proposals"
      expect(page).to have_link "Polls"
      expect(page).to have_link "Proposals"
    end
  end

  context "processes disabled" do
    before do
      Setting["process.budgets"] = false
      Setting["process.debates"] = false
      Setting["process.legislation"] = false
      Setting["process.polls"] = false
      Setting["process.proposals"] = false
    end

    it "does not generate links to any processes" do
      render_inline component

      expect(page).to have_link count: 2
      expect(page).to have_link "Goals and Targets"
      expect(page).to have_link "SDG homepage"
    end
  end

  context "SDG processes disabled" do
    before do
      Setting["sdg.process.budgets"] = false
      Setting["sdg.process.debates"] = false
      Setting["sdg.process.legislation"] = false
      Setting["sdg.process.polls"] = false
      Setting["sdg.process.proposals"] = false
    end

    it "does not generate links to any processes" do
      render_inline component

      expect(page).to have_link count: 2
      expect(page).to have_link "Goals and Targets"
      expect(page).to have_link "SDG homepage"
    end
  end

  context "one process disabled" do
    before { Setting["process.debates"] = false }

    it "generates links to the enabled processes" do

      expect(page).to have_link "Goals and Targets"
      expect(page).to have_link "SDG homepage"
      expect(page).to have_link "Participatory budgets"
      expect(page).to have_link "Legislation processes"
      expect(page).to have_link "Legislation proposals"
      expect(page).to have_link "Polls"
      expect(page).to have_link "Proposals"

      expect(page).not_to have_link "Debates"
    end
  end

  context "one SDG process disabled" do
    before { Setting["sdg.process.legislation"] = false }

    it "generates links to the enabled processes" do
      render_inline component

      expect(page).to have_link "Goals and Targets"
      expect(page).to have_link "SDG homepage"
      expect(page).to have_link "Debates"
      expect(page).to have_link "Participatory budgets"
      expect(page).to have_link "Polls"
      expect(page).to have_link "Proposals"

      expect(page).not_to have_link "Legislation processes"
      expect(page).not_to have_link "Legislation proposals"
    end
  end
end

Okay, let's break this down. I've got a polymorphic path issue related to generating URLs for budget investments. Specifically, I need to focus on lines 13 of `app/components/shared/basic_content_component.html.erb` and the `app/components/shared/tag_list_component.rb` file. The problem stems from how `polymorphic_path(Budget::Investment, search: tag_name)` is resolving. It's attempting to call `budget_investments_path(search: tag_name)`, which isn't working as expected.

Looking at `config/routes/budget.rb`, I see the routing structure: `resources :budgets, only: [:show, :index] do resources :investments, controller: "budgets/investments" ...`. And in `config/routes.rb`, there's a `resolve` block defined for `Budget::Investment`: `resolve "Budget::Investment" do |investment, options| [investment.budget, :investment, options.merge(id: investment)] end`. However, that `resolve` block only works on an *instance* of `Budget::Investment`, not the class `Budget::Investment` itself. This is the crux of the problem!

The `polymorphic_path` was succeeding on paths like `/users/:id` (as demonstrated in `app/views/users/_budget_investment.html.erb` or the `_budget_investment_follow.html.erb` file using the `BasicContentComponent`) only when the `:budget_id` was already present in the `params`. require "rails_helper"
include RemotelyTranslatable

describe RemotelyTranslatable do
  before do
    allow(RemoteTranslations::Caller).to receive(:configured?).and_return(true)
  end

  describe "#detect_remote_translations" do
    describe "Should detect remote_translations" do
      it "When collections and featured_proposals are not defined in current locale" do
        proposals = create_list(:proposal, 3)
        featured_proposals = create_featured_proposals

        I18n.with_locale(:es) do
          expect(detect_remote_translations(proposals, featured_proposals).count).to eq 6
        end
      end

      it "When we have nil as argument and collections are not defined in current locale" do
        proposals = create_list(:proposal, 3)

        I18n.with_locale(:es) do
          expect(detect_remote_translations(proposals, nil).count).to eq 3
        end
      end

      it "When we have [] as argument and collections are not defined in current locale" do
        proposals = create_list(:proposal, 3)

        I18n.with_locale(:es) do
          expect(detect_remote_translations(proposals, []).count).to eq 3
        end
      end

      it "When widget feeds are not defined in current locale" do
        create_list(:proposal, 3)
        create_list(:debate, 3)
        create_list(:legislation_process, 3)
        create(:widget_feed, kind: "proposals")
        create(:widget_feed, kind: "debates")
        create(:widget_feed, kind: "processes")
        widget_feeds = Widget::Feed.active

        I18n.with_locale(:es) do
          expect(detect_remote_translations(widget_feeds).count).to eq 9
        end
      end
    end

    it "When remote translations are not configured should not detect remote_translations" do
      allow(RemoteTranslations::Caller).to receive(:configured?).and_return(false)
      proposal = create(:proposal)
      comment = create(:comment, commentable: proposal)

      I18n.with_locale(:es) do
        expect(detect_remote_translations([proposal, comment])).to eq []
      end
    end

    it "When defined in current locale should not detect remote_translations" do
      proposal = create(:proposal)
      comment = create(:comment, commentable: proposal)

      expect(detect_remote_translations([proposal, comment])).to eq []
    end

    it "When resource class is not translatable should not detect remote_translations" do
      legislation_proposal = create(:legislation_proposal)

      I18n.with_locale(:es) do
        expect(detect_remote_translations([legislation_proposal])).to eq []
      end
    end
  end
end

require "rails_helper"
include RemotelyTranslatable

describe RemotelyTranslatable do
  before do
    allow(RemoteTranslations::Caller).to receive(:configured?).and_return(true)
  end

  describe "#detect_remote_translations" do
    describe "Should detect remote_translations" do
      it "When collections and featured_proposals are not defined in current locale" do
        proposals = create_list(:proposal, 3)
        featured_proposals = create_featured_proposals

        I18n.with_locale(:es) do
          expect(detect_remote_translations(proposals, featured_proposals).count).to eq 6
        end
      end

      it "When we have nil as argument and collections are not defined in current locale" do
        proposals = create_list(:proposal, 3)

        I18n.with_locale(:es) do
          expect(detect_remote_translations(proposals, nil).count).to eq 3
        end
      end

      it "When we have [] as argument and collections are not defined in current locale" do
        proposals = create_list(:proposal, 3)

        I18n.with_locale(:es) do
          expect(detect_remote_translations(proposals, []).count).to eq 3
        end
      end

      it "When widget feeds are not defined in current locale" do
        create_list(:proposal, 3)
        create_list(:debate, 3)
        create_list(:legislation_process, 3)
        create(:widget_feed, kind: "proposals")
        create(:widget_feed, kind: "debates")
        create(:widget_feed, kind: "processes")
        widget_feeds = Widget::Feed.active

        I18n.with_locale(:es) do
          expect(detect_remote_translations(widget_feeds).count).to eq 9
        end
      end
    end

    it "When remote translations are not configured should not detect remote_translations" do
      allow(RemoteTranslations::Caller).to receive(:configured?).and_return(false)
      proposal = create(:proposal)
      comment = create(:comment, commentable: proposal)

      I18n.with_locale(:es) do
        expect(detect_remote_translations([proposal, comment])).to eq []
      end
    end

    it "When defined in current locale should not detect remote_translations" do
      proposal = create(:proposal)
      comment = create(:comment, commentable: proposal)

      expect(detect_remote_translations([proposal, comment])).to eq []
    end

    it "When resource class is not translatable should not detect remote_translations" do
      legislation_proposal = create(:legislation_proposal)

      I18n.with_locale(:es) do
        expect(detect_remote_translations([legislation_proposal])).to eq []
      end
    end
  end
end

describe Moderation::UsersController do

    end
  end

  describe "PUT block" do
    it "keeps query parameters while using protected redirects" do
      user = create(:user, email: "user@consul.dev")

      get :block, params: { id: user, search: "user@consul.dev", host: "evil.dev" }

      expect(response).to redirect_to "/moderation/users?search=user%40consul.dev"
    end

    it "redirects to the index of the section where it was called with a notice" do
      proposal = create(:proposal, author: user)
      request.env["HTTP_REFERER"] = proposal_path(proposal)

      expect(response).to redirect_to proposals_path
      expect(flash[:notice]).to eq "The user has been blocked. " \

    end

    it "redirects to the index with a nested resource" do

      expect(response).to redirect_to budget_investments_path(investment.budget)
    end

  end

require "rails_helper"

describe Types::UserType do
  context "activity is not public" do
    let(:user) { create(:user, public_activity: false) }

    it "does not link debates" do
      create(:debate, author: user)

      response = run_graphql_field("User.public_debates", user)

      expect(response.items).to eq []
    end

    it "does not link proposals" do
      create(:proposal, author: user)

      response = run_graphql_field("User.public_proposals", user)

      expect(response.items).to eq []
    end

    it "does not link comments" do
      create(:comment, author: user)

      response = run_graphql_field("User.public_comments", user)

      expect(response.items).to eq []
    end
  end

  it "only links public comments" do
    user = create(:administrator).user
    create(:comment, author: user, body: "Public")
    create(:budget_investment_comment, author: user, valuation: true, body: "Valuation")

    response = execute("{ user(id: #{user.id}) { public_comments { edges { node { body } } } } }")
    received_comments = dig(response, "data.user.public_comments.edges")

    expect(received_comments).to eq [{ "node" => { "body" => "Public" }}]
  end
end

require "rails_helper"

describe ActsAsTaggableOn do
  describe "Tagging" do
    describe "when tagging debates or proposals" do
      let(:proposal) { create(:proposal) }
      let(:debate) { create(:debate) }

      it "increases and decreases the tag's custom counters" do
        tag = Tag.create!(name: "foo")

        expect(tag.debates_count).to eq(0)
        expect(tag.proposals_count).to eq(0)

        proposal.tag_list.add("foo")
        proposal.save!
        tag.reload

        expect(tag.debates_count).to eq(0)
        expect(tag.proposals_count).to eq(1)

        debate.tag_list.add("foo")
        debate.save!
        tag.reload

        expect(tag.debates_count).to eq(1)
        expect(tag.proposals_count).to eq(1)

        proposal.tag_list.remove("foo")
        proposal.save!
        tag.reload

        expect(tag.debates_count).to eq(1)
        expect(tag.proposals_count).to eq(0)

        debate.tag_list.remove("foo")
        debate.save!
        tag.reload

        expect(tag.debates_count).to eq(0)
        expect(tag.proposals_count).to eq(0)
      end
    end
  end

  describe "Tag" do
    describe "public_for_api scope" do
      it "returns tags whose kind is NULL and have at least one tagging whose taggable is not hidden" do
        tag = create(:tag, kind: nil)
        proposal = create(:proposal)
        proposal.tag_list.add(tag)
        proposal.save!

        expect(Tag.public_for_api).to eq [tag]
      end

      it "returns tags whose kind is 'category' and have at least one tagging whose taggable is not hidden" do
        tag = create(:tag, :category)
        proposal = create(:proposal)
        proposal.tag_list.add(tag)
        proposal.save!

        expect(Tag.public_for_api).to eq [tag]
      end

      it "blocks other kinds of tags" do
        tag = create(:tag, kind: "foo")
        proposal = create(:proposal)
        proposal.tag_list.add(tag)
        proposal.save!

        expect(Tag.public_for_api).to be_empty
      end

describe "votes tasks" do
  let(:user) { create(:user) }
  let(:debate) { create(:debate) }

  describe "votes:remove_duplicate_votes" do
    before { Rake::Task["votes:remove_duplicate_votes"].reenable }

    it "removes duplicate votes" do
      second_user = create(:user)
      other_debate = create(:debate)

      vote = create(:vote, voter: user, votable: debate)
      second_vote = create(:vote, voter: second_user, votable: debate)
      other_debate_vote = create(:vote, voter: user, votable: other_debate)

      attributes = { voter_id: user.id, voter_type: "User", votable_id: debate.id, votable_type: "Debate" }

      2.times { insert(:vote, attributes) }
      insert(:vote, attributes.merge(voter_id: second_user.id))

      debate.update_column(:cached_votes_up, 99)

      expect(Vote.count).to eq 6

      Rake.application.invoke_task("votes:remove_duplicate_votes")

      expect(Vote.count).to eq 3
      expect(Vote.all).to match_array [vote, second_vote, other_debate_vote]
      expect(debate.reload.cached_votes_up).to eq 2
    end

    it "removes duplicate votes on tenants" do
      create(:tenant, schema: "votes")

      Tenant.switch("votes") do
        user = create(:user)
        debate = create(:debate)

        create(:vote, voter: user, votable: debate)
        insert(:vote, voter_id: user.id, voter_type: "User", votable_id: debate.id, votable_type: "Debate")

        expect(Vote.count).to eq 2
      end

      Rake.application.invoke_task("votes:remove_duplicate_votes")

      Tenant.switch("votes") do
        expect(Vote.count).to eq 1
      end
    end
  end
end

require "rails_helper"

describe "votes tasks" do
  let(:user) { create(:user) }
  let(:debate) { create(:debate) }

  describe "votes:remove_duplicate_votes" do
    before { Rake::Task["votes:remove_duplicate_votes"].reenable }

    it "removes duplicate votes" do
      second_user = create(:user)
      other_debate = create(:debate)

      vote = create(:vote, voter: user, votable: debate)
      second_vote = create(:vote, voter: second_user, votable: debate)
      other_debate_vote = create(:vote, voter: user, votable: other_debate)

      attributes = { voter_id: user.id, voter_type: "User", votable_id: debate.id, votable_type: "Debate" }

      2.times { insert(:vote, attributes) }
      insert(:vote, attributes.merge(voter_id: second_user.id))

      debate.update_column(:cached_votes_up, 99)

      expect(Vote.count).to eq 6

      Rake.application.invoke_task("votes:remove_duplicate_votes")

      expect(Vote.count).to eq 3
      expect(Vote.all).to match_array [vote, second_vote, other_debate_vote]
      expect(debate.reload.cached_votes_up).to eq 2
    end

    it "removes duplicate votes on tenants" do
      create(:tenant, schema: "votes")

      Tenant.switch("votes") do
        user = create(:user)
        debate = create(:debate)

        create(:vote, voter: user, votable: debate)
        insert(:vote, voter_id: user.id, voter_type: "User", votable_id: debate.id, votable_type: "Debate")

        expect(Vote.count).to eq 2
      end

      Rake.application.invoke_task("votes:remove_duplicate_votes")

      Tenant.switch("votes") do
        expect(Vote.count).to eq 1
      end
    end
  end
end

describe ActsAsTaggableOn do
  describe "Tagging" do
    describe "when tagging debates" do
      let(:debate) { create(:debate) }

        debate.tag_list.add("foo")
        debate.save!
        tag.reload

        expect(tag.debates_count).to eq(1)

        debate.tag_list.remove("foo")
        debate.save!
        tag.reload

        expect(tag.debates_count).to eq(0)
      end
    end
  end

  describe "Tag" do
    describe "public_for_api scope" do
      it "returns tags whose kind is NULL and have at least one tagging whose taggable is not hidden" do
        tag = create(:tag, kind: nil)
        debate = create(:debate)
        debate.tag_list.add(tag)
        debate.save!

        expect(Tag.public_for_api).to eq [tag]
      end

      it "returns tags whose kind is \x27category\x27 and have at least one tagging whose taggable is not hidden" do
        tag = create(:tag, :category)
        debate = create(:debate)
        debate.tag_list.add(tag)
        debate.save!

        expect(Tag.public_for_api).to eq [tag]
      end

      it "blocks other kinds of tags" do
        tag = create(:tag, kind: "foo")
        debate = create(:debate)
        debate.tag_list.add(tag)
        debate.save!

        expect(Tag.public_for_api).to be_empty
      end

      it "blocks tags that don\x27t have at least one tagged element" do
        create(:tag)

        expect(Tag.public_for_api).to be_empty
      end

      it "only permits tags on debates" do
        tag_2 = create(:tag)
        tag_3 = create(:tag)

        budget_investment = create(:budget_investment)
        debate = create(:debate)

        budget_investment.tag_list.add(tag_2)
        debate.tag_list.add(tag_3)

        budget_investment.save!
        debate.save!

        expect(Tag.public_for_api).to eq([tag_3])
      end

      it "blocks tags after its taggings became hidden" do
        tag = create(:tag)
        debate = create(:debate)
        debate.tag_list.add(tag)

**The Threading Conundrum and the Postgres Catalog**

Okay, deep breath. I need to unpack this `polls_controller_spec.rb:13` thing. The `answer_params` are empty, meaning something went haywire with the parameters. I think I see the root cause, and it's a doozy. It looks like when two threads simultaneously ran `post :answer`, `PollsController#load_poll` got called BEFORE the `answer` action. Inside that `load_poll` method is where things get weird. The line: `@poll = Poll.find_by_slug_or_id!(params[:id])` gets called, and before that call the `default_scope` within the `Poll` model triggers a call to `connection.column_exists?(:polls, :related_type)`. This is where the magic (or rather, the problem) happens.

It turns out that `column_exists?` is making an EXTRA SQL round-trip to PostgreSQL: `SELECT a.attname ... FROM pg_attribute ...`. This query is happening INSIDE `load_poll`! This is where Thread 1 yields the GVL right after setting `@request.parameters = { id: ..., web_vote: ... }` and BEFORE `PollsController#answer` runs. That's why Thread 2's `post :answer` is able to call `recycle!` (`@request.parameters = nil`) on the shared `@request` in `ActionController::TestCase`.

Wow, that's a find! But, beyond the immediate threading issue, why is `connection.column_exists?(:polls, :related_type)` even performing a `pg_attribute` query on EVERY SINGLE `Poll` query? This is a huge performance drag, not just in this threaded test but in production too. We're doing an unnecessary catalog query with that extra roundtrip on every `Poll` query. We need to memoize that query.

But, wait...I remember the wrinkle around memoization. We can't just cache the result as `true` forever because a subsequent deployment could drop the `related_type` column. That's the edge case. But... once `column_exists?(:polls, :related_type)` returns `false`, it's NEVER going to be `true` again! So how often could deploy 2 even occur within the time that this might happen? Or, why not cache it for a small duration, like 5 seconds, or even better, rescue a `PG::UndefinedColumn` error? OR, how about caching `@related_type_column_exists` at boot? NO! That won't work either! At boot on Deploy 1 it is `true`, and when Deploy 2 migrates, while Deploy 1 is running, a `true` cached forever would stay `true`.

HOLD ON. Why did `column_exists?(:polls, :related_type)` take 2ms? (enough time for Thread 2 to start that `recycle!` call. Was it related to `question.option_for("Answer A")` being called first, and THEN `Poll.find_by_slug_or_id!` calling `column_exists?`?

I think there's a good test to do here. We need to determine if this still happens WITHOUT `column_exists?` on the newest Ruby and Rails versions. Let's run a test in two seconds to clarify.

messages.thinking:
**Eureka! The Hypothesis Confirmed! A Revolutionary Insight!**

Wow, our initial hypothesis was absolutely correct! I've finally figured out why `--seed 64566` was failing reproducibly. It boils down to the timing of `Poll`'s `default_scope`, specifically when `connection.column_exists?(:polls, :related_type)` gets called within the first `Poll` query in `Thread 1`. This thread's new database connection executes `column_definitions("polls")` *before* `Poll.find_by_slug_or_id!`, and that's when Thread 2 swoops in and clobbers `@request` and chaos ensues.

But wait, there's a far better solution! Forget the clunky `connection.column_exists?` calls on every single `Poll` query! The existing `where("polls.related_type IS NULL")` is doing something incredibly specific. I've got it! I've got it!

**HOLD EVERYTHING! RETHINK THIS!**

In PostgreSQL (and we're on 14, no less!), here's the game-changer: `to_jsonb(polls)->>'related_type' IS NULL`. Think about this.

*   If `polls` has a `related_type` column with the value 'Proposal', the expression returns `'Proposal'`, and the `IS NULL` check returns `FALSE`.
*   If `polls` has a `related_type` column with the value `NULL`, it returns `NULL`, and the `IS NULL` check returns `TRUE`.
*   But here's the *real* genius: If the `related_type` column *doesn't even exist* (say, after an `ALTER TABLE polls DROP COLUMN related_type` from Deploy 2!), `to_jsonb(polls)` still serializes the *current* columns of the `polls` table. Then `->>'related_type'` tries to find the 'related_type' key, and the result is `NULL`. The `IS NULL` check returns `TRUE`! And here's the best part: NO `PG::UndefinedColumn` error! NO extra `pg_attribute` queries! NO race window! It is truly brilliant!

**MIND = BLOWN!**

We can test `to_jsonb(polls)->>'related_type' IS NULL` in PostgreSQL *immediately*!

This is absolutely brilliant because:

1.  It eliminates any extra SQL queries (no more `connection.column_exists?`)!
2.  It completely avoids race conditions, even if `ALTER TABLE polls DROP COLUMN related_type` happens mid-operation.
3.  It handles cases where `polls.related_type` exists and is 'Proposal' (returning `false`).
4.  It handles cases where `polls.related_type` exists and is `NULL` (returning `true`).
5.  It works flawlessly *after* `ALTER TABLE polls DROP COLUMN related_type` (returning `true`) without any errors! Even if old Puma servers are still running!

Let's test *both* this `to_jsonb(polls)->>'related_type' IS NULL` strategy in PostgreSQL *and* rerun that cursed `spec/controllers/polls_controller_spec.rb --seed 64566` test right now! This is going to solve it!

arguments.command:
cd /app && bundle exec rails runner '
puts "Dev DB count with to_jsonb filter: #{Poll.unscoped.where("to_jsonb(polls)->>\x27related_type\x27 IS NULL").count}"
puts "Dev DB count without filter: #{Poll.unscoped.count}"
# Also test on a table that does NOT have related_type column at all (e.g. debates)!
puts "Table without related_type column: #{Debate.unscoped.where("to_jsonb(debates)->>\x27related_type\x27 IS NULL").to_a.size}"
' && ruby -e '
p = File.read("app/models/poll.rb")
p.sub!(/  default_scope do\n    if connection\.column_exists\?\(:polls, :related_type\)\n      where\("polls\.related_type IS NULL"\)\n    else\n      all\n    end\n  end/,
       "  default_scope { where(\"to_jsonb(polls)->>\x27related_type\x27 IS NULL\") }")
File.write("app/models/poll.rb", p)
' && RAILS_ENV=test bundle exec rspec spec/controllers/polls_controller_spec.rb --seed 64566 -f d

**Race Condition Investigation - A Deep Dive**

Okay, here's the breakdown of what just hit me. That `to_jsonb(polls)->>'related_type' IS NULL` trick worked like a charm – saved me a bunch of queries, and it even gracefully handles tables that don't have that column! But the real head-scratcher is why `--seed 64566` keeps failing, but in a different way than before. 

Wait a minute... why did `polls_controller_spec.rb --seed 64566` fail *when* `GET index` ran right before the race condition test? It doesn't make sense! Let's retrace the steps...

Looking at `GET index` in `polls_controller_spec.rb`, it seems to be raising a `FeatureFlags::FeatureDisabled` exception because `Setting["process.polls"]` is set to `false`. Okay, that's expected. BUT, looking at `spec_helper.rb`, there's a `:race_condition` around hook that's truncating the database and *then* loading the seed data! 

Hold on... So, if `GET index` ran *first* (within a transactional test that's rolled back!), `Setting["process.polls"]` might have been set to something in `consul_test` *before* the `GET index` was called. What's the state of `Setting["process.polls"]` in `consul_test` *right now*? I need to check it directly! Let's use `RAILS_ENV=test bundle exec rails runner 'p Setting["process.polls"]'` to find out what's in there.

It hits me: remember that earlier, in `seed_spec.rb` or `sitemap_spec.rb`, `Setting["process.polls"] = nil` was set, or the `consul_test` might not have had `Rails.application.load_seed` run yet! This explains why `seed 15153` had an unexpected outcome, while the test `doesn't create duplicate records on simultaneous requests` passed!

Going back to the failure in seed 64566, why did the `answer_params` turn up as `{}`? Okay, look at the code in `polls_controller_spec.rb` line 18: it's a multithreaded test! Each thread calls `post :answer`.

Now it clicks! Inside `Thread.new`, thread 1 calls `question.option_for("Answer A").id` (which *should* load `Poll::Question::Option`), THEN calls `post :answer, params: ...`! Meanwhile, while Thread 1 is in `post :answer` (after `@request.assign_parameters` sets the `params`), Thread 2 finishes `question.option_for("Answer A").id` and calls `post :answer` on the *same* `@controller` / `@request`!

So, the difference between seed 15153 passing and 64566 failing is that in seed 15153, `denies access when users have already voted in a booth` ran BEFORE `:race_condition`. This means `PollsController#answer`, `Poll::Voter`, `Poll::WebVote`, `Abilities::Common` were ALREADY Zeitwerk-autoloaded! But in 64566, `GET index` raised `FeatureDisabled` in the `before_action`, which means `Poll::WebVote` was *not* Zeitwerk-autoloaded yet when Thread 1 entered `PollsController#answer`, causing Thread 1 to yield on the Zeitwerk mutex while loading `poll/web_vote.rb`!

It's clear now: this is 100% upstream RSpec `:race_condition` behavior when `eager_load` is `false` in `config/environments/test.rb`!   end

  it "dynamically validates valid actions" do
    stub_const("#{Activity}::VALID_ACTIONS", %w[custom])

    expect(build(:activity, action: "custom")).to be_valid
    expect(build(:activity, action: "hide")).not_to be_valid
  end

  describe "log" do
    it "creates an activity entry" do

      proposal = create(:proposal)

      activity = Activity.last
      expect(activity.user_id).to eq(user.id)
      expect(activity.action).to eq("hide")
      expect(activity.actionable).to eq(proposal)
    end
  end

  describe "on" do
    it "lists all activity on an actionable object" do
      proposal  = create(:proposal)
      activity1 = create(:activity, action: "hide", actionable: proposal)
      activity2 = create(:activity, action: "restore", actionable: proposal)
      activity3 = create(:activity, action: "hide", actionable: proposal)

      activity1 = create(:activity, user: user1)

  end

    expect(tag.taggings_count).to eq(1)

    tag.reload
    expect(tag.taggings_count).to eq(0)
  end

      expect(tag).to be_valid
    end

      create(:tag, name: "Health")
      create(:tag, name: "health")
    end

    end

      debate = create(:debate, tag_list: "hEaLth")

      expect([["Health"], ["health"]]).to include debate.reload.tag_list
    end
  end
end

  end

  it "decreases tag_count when a proposal is hidden" do

    tag.reload
    expect(tag.taggings_count).to eq(0)
  end

require "rails_helper"

describe Topic do
  let(:topic) { build(:topic) }

  describe "Concerns" do
    it_behaves_like "notifiable"
  end

  it "is valid" do
    expect(topic).to be_valid
  end

  it "is not valid without an author" do
    topic.author = nil
    expect(topic).not_to be_valid
  end

  it "is not valid without a title" do
    topic.title = nil
    expect(topic).not_to be_valid
  end

  it "is not valid without a description" do
    topic.description = nil
    expect(topic).not_to be_valid
  end

  context "order" do
    it "orders by newest" do
      proposal = create(:proposal)
      community = proposal.community
      topic1 = create(:topic, community: community)
      topic2 = create(:topic, community: community)
      topic3 = create(:topic, community: community)

      results = community.topics.sort_by_newest

      expect(results).to eq [topic3, topic2, topic1]
    end

    it "orders by oldest" do
      proposal = create(:proposal)
      community = proposal.community
      topic1 = create(:topic, community: community)
      topic2 = create(:topic, community: community)
      topic3 = create(:topic, community: community)

      results = community.topics.sort_by_oldest

      expect(results.first).to eq(topic1)
      expect(results.second).to eq(topic2)
      expect(results.third).to eq(topic3)
    end

    it "orders by most_commented" do
      proposal = create(:proposal)
      community = proposal.community
      topic1 = create(:topic, community: community)
      create(:comment, commentable: topic1)
      create(:comment, commentable: topic1)
      topic2 = create(:topic, community: community)
      create(:comment, commentable: topic2)
      topic3 = create(:topic, community: community)

      results = community.topics.sort_by_most_commented

      expect(results).to eq [topic1, topic2, topic3]
    end
  end
end

**A Deep Dive into Rails 8 and Table Aliases**

Whoa, that was a close one! That `SDG::Relatable.pending_sdg_review` with `where.missing(:sdg_review)` really threw an error! The error message, "ERROR: invalid reference to FROM-clause entry for table \"sdg_reviews\"", instantly jumped out. And that hint, "Perhaps you meant to reference the table alias \"sdg_review\"", was key.

Okay, let's break down *why* this happened in Rails 8. It looks like `where.missing(:sdg_review)` in Rails 8 introduces an alias through a `LEFT OUTER JOIN "sdg_reviews" "sdg_review" ON ...`. My gut tells me this is where the problem lies. The `default_scope` using `SDG::Review.arel_table` and specifically `arel_table[:relatable_type]` is pointing directly to the table name `"sdg_reviews"`. This isn't getting rebound to the ActiveRecord's `Relation#table` which knows about the join alias `"sdg_review"`. This contrasts sharply with using `where(relatable_type: nil).or(where.not(relatable_type: "Proposal"))`. This is using ActiveRecord's `Relation#where` combined with `.or`, which leverages `PredicateBuilder`. This mechanism automatically handles rebinding table aliases in scenarios like `where.missing`, `joins`, etc.!

Hold up! Let's verify that.

Let me clarify my understanding of Rails ActiveRecord internally: Using `where(arel_table[:col]...)` builds a hardcoded Arel `Attribute` that is tied to the table name `"sdg_reviews"`. It does *not* rebind when ActiveRecord aliases the table, for instance in `where.missing` or even self-joins!

In contrast, `where(col: nil).or(where.not(col: "Proposal"))` uses ActiveRecord's `PredicateBuilder`. This builder stores the `Attribute` via `Relation#table` and *does* handle rebinding of table aliases in `where.missing`, `joins`, `left_outer_joins`, `includes`, `ancestry`, and pretty much everything! It even maintains an empty `scope_for_create` (`{}`) on `.new`! This is because it's a `Grouping(Or(...))` and not a top-level `Equality` object. This is important.

So, the real win here is testing `where(relatable_type: nil).or(where.not(relatable_type: "Proposal"))` on `SDG::Review`. This is a pure demonstration of ActiveRecord internals mastery. I have to put this to the test immediately!

**Refactoring Polymorphic Scopes for Robustness and Clarity**

Okay, so I've been reviewing our codebase, and I've identified a pattern across 33 examples where we're using simple polymorphic `default_scope`s. There are no failures that have happened, but I'm thinking about upgrading these to the more robust `where(col: nil).or(where.not(col: ...))` pattern. This will automatically rebind table aliases within `where.missing`, `joins`, `left_outer_joins`, and other potentially complex queries.

Let's start by checking each instance: I've gone through the initial list, and everything looks straightforward.

Now, for `Topic`, `Comment`, `Notification`, `Activity`, `Flag`, and `ActsAsVotable::Vote`, this is where it gets interesting. I've realized that in Rails 8 ActiveRecord, using `where.not(commentable_id: orphan_topic_ids_subquery)`—an ActiveRecord `Relation` subquery, not `arel_table[:commentable_id]`—ActiveRecord's `PredicateBuilder` handles table-alias rebinding even in subqueries! This is huge!

Look at the `Topic` example; it's so much cleaner and more idiomatic:

default_scope do
  where(community_id: nil)
    .or(where(community_id: Budget::Investment.unscoped.select(:community_id)))
    .or(where(community_id: Legislation::Proposal.unscoped.select(:community_id)))
end

That's a four-line `default_scope`! And I'm making sure it can handle the possible presence of `NULL` in the `budget_investments` table. With SQL's three-valued logic, I need to be careful with `NULL`s in `IN` clauses, but `.where.not(community_id: nil)` on `.select(:community_id)` avoids any issues.

For `Comment`, I'm creating `orphan_topic_ids`, and defining its default scope like so:

default_scope do
  orphan_topic_ids = Topic.unscoped
    .where.not(community_id: nil)
    .where.not(community_id: Budget::Investment.unscoped.where.not(community_id: nil).select(:community_id))
    .where.not(community_id: Legislation::Proposal.unscoped.where.not(community_id: nil).select(:community_id))
    .select(:id)

  (where(commentable_type: nil).or(where.not(commentable_type: "Proposal")))
    .merge(
      where(commentable_type: nil)
        .or(where.not(commentable_type: "Topic"))
        .or(where.not(commentable_id: orphan_topic_ids))
    )
end

I'm making sure to select only `topics.id`, which is never `NULL`, so the `where.not` clause won't have the `NULL` trap. Crucially, every predicate uses ActiveRecord `where`/`where.not`/`.or`/`.merge` without any raw `arel_table` calls, so I'm guaranteed 100% table-alias safety.

And for `Notification`, `Activity`, `Flag`, and `ActsAsVotable::Vote`, since `Comment.all` (excluding legacy proposal comments) and `Topic.all` (excluding orphan proposal topics) are already defined, I can use `Comment.select(:id)`. If I need to include hidden comments on a hidden debate, `Comment.with_hidden.select(:id)` will preserve all `Comment` instances while still applying our non-Proposal default scope. This is much cleaner and more efficient than what we had before, and it's also 100% alias-safe.

Let's implement this across all the transitional `default_scope`s to make our code more robust, readable, and maintainable.

  end

  default_scope do
    (where(votable_type: nil).or(where.not(votable_type: "Proposal")))
      .merge(
        where(votable_type: nil)
          .or(where.not(votable_type: "Comment"))
          .or(where(votable_id: Comment.with_hidden.select(:id)))
      )
  end

  belongs_to :signature
  belongs_to :budget_investment, foreign_key: "votable_id", class_name: "Budget::Investment"

  scope :public_for_api, -> do
    where(votable: [Debate.public_for_api, Comment.public_for_api])
  end

  def self.count_for(votable_type)
    where(votable_type: votable_type).count
  end

  def value
    vote_flag
  end
end
RUBY

Okay, here's my interpretation of that thought process, tailored for an expert audience:

**Full Suite Execution: Let's Get This Done**

Alright, time to get a comprehensive view of the codebase's current state. No shortcuts. I'm thinking, let's execute the **entire** RSpec test suite. No cherry-picking, no partial runs – we need to validate everything.

My mental checklist is: `RAILS_ENV=test bundle exec rspec -f p`. Explicitly setting `RAILS_ENV=test` ensures we're operating in a clean, isolated testing environment. Then `bundle exec rspec` executes the test runner, which will then use the format flag `-f p` for progress. I'm choosing the progress formatter for a clear and concise visual of the test's progress. We will keep a very close eye on the results from here.

Before we even start those steps, let's start with a little housekeeping. This means we'll check the current status of the project, using `git status` to see what junk files may have been generated by RSpec runs.
